newsitem.title: JAPAN: Earthquake hits southwest Japan, no damage reported.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake hits southwest Japan, no damage reported.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 5.9 on the Richter scale shook wide areas of southwestern Japan on Wednesday, but there were no immediate reports of damage or casualties, the Meteorological Agency said.
The tremor occured at 6.50 p.m. (0950 GMT), the agency said.
The epicentre of the earthquake was 20 km (12.5 miles) underground near Yamaguchi prefecture, which is 782 km (489 miles) southwest of Tokyo, it said.
The quake registered five on the Japanese scale of seven in western Japan's Shimane prefecture, 600 km (380 miles) west of Tokyo.
Railway authorities said they briefly suspended Shinkansen bullet train services in the areas as a precautionary measure.
A local government official in Shimane said the earthquake shook the prefectural government building for several minutes.
"The building was shaking for several minutes. But no objects or documents fell off their shelves," the official told Reuters by telephone.
A tremor with a magnitude of six on the Richter scale is strong enough to cause heavy damage to buildings, roads and other facilities in populated areas.
There was no possibility of the earthquake triggering tidal waves, it added.
